claim: D1's conditional-write protocol has no branch for a bucket that exists WITHOUT a version attribute, which is every pre-cutover bucket including the backfill's primary targets. D1 offers exactly two conditions: 'version = :expected' (requires a version to have been read) and 'attribute_not_exists(PK) for creation' (fails because the item exists). A legacy bucket satisfies neither, so under the protocol as written every backfill write against a pre-cutover bucket fails ConditionalCheckFailed into the manifest failures list (the backfill cannot rewrite the very buckets it exists to repair), and every live accumulation into a same-day pre-cutover bucket in the deploy-to-backfill gap exhausts its bounded retries and is lost to the FR-009 repair path. The Clarifications session says '(or attribute_not_exists for new buckets)' without naming the attribute, and data-model's state machine 'absent -> created -> accumulating' omits the present-but-unversioned state entirely
evidence: research.md D1 'ConditionExpression: version = :expected or attribute_not_exists(PK) for creation'; data-model.md:33 'write accepted only at expected version' and :36-38 state transitions; contracts/bucket-schema.md 'version is present on every bucket written after cutover' (so pre-cutover buckets lack it); spec.md Clarifications Q4
proposed_resolution: Add the third branch explicitly in D1, data-model validation rules, and the state machine: when the read found no version attribute, condition the write on attribute_not_exists(version); reserve attribute_not_exists(PK) for absent buckets. State that legacy-unversioned is a first-class pre-state for both live path and backfill

claim: D2's supporting code claim is false: 'SSE does not import timeseries fanout'. SSE imports the src.lib.timeseries package (sse_streaming/handler.py:42, stream.py:42, polling.py:231), and src/lib/timeseries/__init__.py imports write_fanout and write_fanout_with_update from fanout.py at package-import time, so every SSE cold start transitively imports the fanout module. The placement decision survives for a different, unstated reason: the SSE Dockerfile copies lib/timeseries as a whole directory (COPY lib/timeseries /var/task/src/lib/timeseries), so signed.py inside the package ships to SSE. The real constraint D2 should state: fanout.py/signed.py must not import top-level src/lib modules other than metrics.py, the only top-level lib file the SSE image copies (fanout.py:21 imports src.lib.metrics, which is copied; anything else breaks SSE at cold start, the exact docs/ci-gotchas.md:67-84 failure mode)
evidence: src/lib/timeseries/__init__.py imports write_fanout/write_fanout_with_update; sse_streaming/handler.py:42, stream.py:42, polling.py:231; sse_streaming/Dockerfile COPY lib/timeseries and COPY lib/metrics.py lines; research.md D2 rationale
proposed_resolution: Correct D2's rationale: SSE transitively imports fanout via the package __init__; safety comes from the directory-level COPY of lib/timeseries plus fanout's out-of-package imports staying within lib/metrics.py. State that invariant as the design constraint

claim: The plan's change set omits src/lib/timeseries/__init__.py, whose edit is mandatory: D7 deletes write_fanout and write_fanout_with_update, but __init__.py imports both and exports both in __all__, and the analysis handler imports write_fanout through the package (handler.py:78). Deleting the functions without touching __init__.py raises ImportError at import time for every consumer of the package, including SSE (which never calls fanout but executes the import at cold start). The plan's Source Code tree lists fanout.py, models.py, signed.py, handler.py, sentiment.py only
evidence: plan.md Project Structure source tree; src/lib/timeseries/__init__.py import and __all__ entries for write_fanout/write_fanout_with_update; src/lambdas/analysis/handler.py:78 'from src.lib.timeseries import SentimentScore, write_fanout'
proposed_resolution: Add src/lib/timeseries/__init__.py to the plan's change list (drop the deleted symbols, export accumulate_fanout and label_to_signed); note the SSE cold-start blast radius as the reason it cannot be left to chance

claim: Audit-trail gap for targeted repairs: quickstart's FR-009 repair invokes the backfill with --ticker <T> --window <iso>, but the manifest contract has no field recording ticker scoping. A targeted run's manifest is indistinguishable from a full-horizon run over the same window, so FR-004's 'windows covered' audit under-describes what was mutated, and cross-run per_resolution count comparisons are meaningless without knowing the scope. Only forced and dry_run flags are recorded; the third CLI dimension (scope) is not
evidence: quickstart.md repair section '--ticker <T> --window <iso>'; contracts/backfill-manifest.md field list (window {from,to} only, no ticker/scope field)
proposed_resolution: Add a scope field to the manifest (e.g. ticker_filter: null | [tickers]) and record the full argv; state that per_resolution comparisons only hold between runs of identical scope

claim: The clarified is_partial contract is absent from the consumer contract where it belongs: bucket-schema.md never mentions is_partial. The Clarifications answer (every write sets True; stored False means explicitly complete; readers compute completeness at query time) made it into data-model.md's attribute table but not into the contract that consumers are told they 'may rely on'. A consumer author reading only the contract could trust the stored flag, which is exactly the mistake dashboard/timeseries.py:129-131 exists to avoid
evidence: contracts/bucket-schema.md (no is_partial line); spec.md Clarifications Q1; data-model.md is_partial row
proposed_resolution: Add an is_partial bullet to bucket-schema.md: stored True is meaningless for completeness (writer always sets it), stored False is authoritative-complete, completeness is otherwise computed from window end vs now

claim: The clarified 240s drain criterion measures Invocations only and does not bound Lambda's async retry queue. Analysis is invoked asynchronously by SNS (main.tf:1065 subscription), reserved_concurrency=5 (main.tf:386), so a throttled or errored pre-disable event can sit in the async queue and be redelivered minutes to hours after 240 seconds of invocation silence, landing mid-backfill. The version condition catches only the clobber direction (backfill write on a stale version fails into the manifest); the other direction is silent: a delayed fanout for an item the backfill already recomputed re-accumulates it on top of the fresh bucket with a valid version read, a double-count that nothing detects and SC-004's quiesced-conditions caveat silently excuses
evidence: spec.md Clarifications Q3 'No analysis Lambda invocations for 240 seconds... checked via CloudWatch Invocations metric'; infrastructure/terraform/main.tf:382-386 (timeout 120, reserved_concurrency 5), :1065 SNS subscription; Lambda async invocation retry/max-event-age semantics
proposed_resolution: Extend the drain criterion: after rule disable, also require AsyncEventsReceived=0 and AsyncEventAge empty over the drain window (or set the analysis function's maximum event age below the drain window for the duration); document the residual double-count direction and its detection (post-backfill spot recompute per SC-003)

claim: FR-004's role scope sentence drifted behind the clarified protocol and D6: it says 'scoped to reading the items table and writing the timeseries table', but Clarification Q4's read-modify-conditional-write requires READING the timeseries table (D6 correctly grants GetItem), and D6 additionally grants events:DescribeRule/DisableRule/EnableRule and cloudwatch:GetMetricData for quiescence. A role built to FR-004's letter cannot execute the clarified protocol or the preflight
evidence: spec.md FR-004 'scoped to reading the items table and writing the timeseries table'; research.md D6 grant list; spec.md Clarifications Q4 'Read each bucket'
proposed_resolution: Amend FR-004's scope sentence to 'reading the items table, reading and writing the timeseries table, and operating the quiescence controls (ingestion rule disable/enable, CloudWatch metric read)' or reference D6 as the authoritative grant list

claim: D6's 'least-privilege set' includes cloudwatch:GetMetricData, which supports no resource-level scoping and must be granted on Resource '*' (account-wide metric read). Not a defect in the choice, but the decision record claims least privilege without stating this residual, which is the first thing a role review will bounce on
evidence: research.md D6 grant list; AWS IAM: cloudwatch:GetMetricData does not support resource-level permissions
proposed_resolution: State in D6 that GetMetricData is necessarily account-wide and accepted as the drain-check cost; keep every other grant resource-scoped (rule ARN, two table ARNs)

claim: D4's plan to 'increment the existing TimeseriesFanoutErrors metric with a window dimension added' changes the metric's identity: dimensions are part of a CloudWatch metric's identity, so dimensioned emissions create new series and anything watching the undimensioned TimeseriesFanoutErrors stops seeing failures; per-window dimension values also create unbounded custom-metric cardinality (each distinct window is a billed series). The structured log already carries the window and D4 itself names Logs Insights as the repair-discovery path, so the dimension is redundant
evidence: research.md D4; src/lambdas/analysis/handler.py:502-503 existing undimensioned emission (per ar1-005 evidence)
proposed_resolution: Keep TimeseriesFanoutErrors undimensioned; rely on the structured log record for window identification

claim: The version guard binds cooperating writers only, and the dormant ingestion-role grant remains a bypass: iam/main.tf:113-132 still grants BatchWriteItem/PutItem/UpdateItem on the timeseries table to the ingestion role (drop deferred to owner per ar1-009). Any unconditional write through it ignores the version condition entirely and, worse under the new schema, strips the version attribute, which under ar2-001's protocol then wedges subsequent conditional writes on that bucket. The Clarifications' 'a quiescence violation fails loudly' holds only for writers that opt into the condition
evidence: infrastructure/terraform/modules/iam/main.tf:113-132; spec.md Clarifications Q4; spec.md Context dormant-grant note
proposed_resolution: State in the spec/research that optimistic concurrency is cooperative, not enforced; re-flag the ingestion grant drop as the enforcement half of the version mechanism rather than optional adjacent hardening (still owner's call)

claim: The quickstart smoke query inspects the wrong end of the range: 'aws dynamodb query ... --max-items 3' returns the OLDEST three NVDA#1h buckets (ascending SK is the query default), and 1h buckets live 7 days, so for a week post-cutover the smoke shows pre-cutover unversioned buckets and reads as cutover failure. Fails safe (false alarm, not false pass) but wastes the operator's gate check
evidence: quickstart.md smoke step 1; DynamoDB Query ScanIndexForward default true; data-model.md TTL note (1h resolution short TTL per models.py ttl map)
proposed_resolution: Add --no-scan-index-forward to the smoke query so the newest buckets return first

claim: backfill-manifest.md's idempotency sentence is internally inconsistent: 'per_resolution counts may differ only in buckets_skipped_ttl' is impossible, because a window that ages across the TTL boundary between runs moves from written to skipped, changing buckets_written by the same amount. Written and skipped counts co-vary by conservation
proposed_resolution: Reword: buckets_written + buckets_skipped_ttl is stable per resolution across quiesced runs over an unchanged item set; the split between them may shift as windows age
